### Summary

This section keeps the selector of the fourth-order reference and its guards; the construction itself, the
five-cell filter, its cubic wall continuation and the four-cell face rule, is derived in @sec-ch05-wbref4 and is
not repeated here.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects the fourth-order, cell/face-consistent density reference of the well-balanced $x_1$
reconstruction; the filter is @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref and its face rule @eq-ch05-wbref4-face (@sec-ch05-wbref4).

**Data.** In: the cell ratios $\chi=\rho/p$ of the owned cells and, across a seam, the exchanged ghost rows;
out: the cell and face density references the reconstruction subtracts and restores.

**Placement.** Inside `HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1`, on every hydro call before the $x_1$ perturbation
reconstruction.

**Activation.** `SNAP_WB_REF4`, default off; on whenever `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is on. With nonzero
`grav1` the setup requires `nghost` at least 3.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact for cubic $\chi$ on a uniform grid; a stencil that is not usable (fewer than four
owned cells next to a clamped wall, fewer than five cells) or a face value outside its cell range keeps the base
reference of @sec-ch05-refkernel.

**Evidence.** `test_wb_ref4_order_python`: three-resolution slope at least `ORDER_ON` = 2.75 with the switch
on and below `ORDER_OFF` = 2.5 with it off, both arms with FC on
({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py ORDER_ON >}}); `test_x1_seam_split_wb_ref4.<b>`: a split column matches
one block to $10^{-13}$ and fewer than three ghosts are refused
({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.wb_ref4_flag_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block >}}); check
`[C2]` of `configuration_check.py`; the ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

### Derivation

See @sec-ch05-wbref4 for the reference filter, the wall continuation and the face rule. The chapter's own check
line `[C2]` re-derives the moment identities independently: the weights $(-1,4,10,4,-1)/16$ have unit zeroth
moment and vanishing first three moments, the cubic wall continuation reproduces every cubic, and the face rule
integrates the quartic interpolant exactly [check `src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

The switch is read once per process by `wb_ref4_enabled` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}),
which also returns true when `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` does. With nonzero $g_1$ the setup of the hydro
module refuses fewer than three ghost cells (`HydroImpl::reset`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}),
because the resolution flag reads pressures three cells away; with zero gravity no reference is built and the
guard is inactive. `wb_ref4_stencils` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}}) builds the stencils
once per grid and marks them usable only with at least five cells and, next to a clamped wall, at least four
owned cells; a block between two seams reads its exchanged ghosts instead. `wb_ref4_cells`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_cells >}}) applies the cell filter and dilates the resolution flag by two
cells, and `wb_ref4_faces` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}) the face rule after the seam
exchange of the cell reference, each keeping the base reference where the stencil is unusable or a value leaves
its cell range. Both run inside `HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}})
with the wall-clamp flags of @sec-ch11-wb.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch12-wb-reference-flow
#| fig-cap: "Five-cell reference filter: sky-blue circles are cell ratios, black ticks are faces, and labels give filter and wall-continuation weights."
#| fig-alt: "five cells: -1,4,10,4,-1; wall: cubic continuation; cell density reference; four-cell face integral."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch12.fig_wb_reference_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Implementation sites for the fourth-order reference selector. {#tbl-ch12-wb-reference-code}

1. Read the switch once, or inherit it from XC. The anchor `wb_ref4_enabled` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}.
2. At setup with gravity, refuse fewer than three ghosts. The anchor `nghost` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}.
3. On each hydro call build or reuse the stencils, apply the cell filter, exchange the seam rows, apply the
   face rule. The anchor `wb_ref4` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}.

The thresholds are `ORDER_ON` and `ORDER_OFF` ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py ORDER_ON >}},

({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py main >}}); the seam assertions are
{{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.wb_ref4_flag_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block >}} and
{{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.wb_ref4_gravity_0_nghost_1_steps >}}; the switched arms are
registered in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
No fitted order is measured here. The guards can lower the effective order near walls and seams, and the
interior moments say nothing about wall or gnomonic convergence. Gnomonic grids and the wider switch combinations
are gaps in @sec-ch12-matrix.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
